events.continuity_hook: The booked coastal trip remains intact except for a material return-flight schedule change that affects the final day and rental-car timing.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the revised Monday itineraries by elapsed time, added fare, connection risk, Carmel departure time, and car-return window; then choose the option that best preserves the final day within the remaining trip budget.
events.scenario_brief: Three weeks before the Monterey Peninsula trip, the airline has moved the Monday San Jose departure from 1:20 p.m. to 10:35 a.m. The new time would require leaving Carmel before 7:00 a.m. and giving up the planned final breakfast and walk. The Thursday outbound, both hotels, whale-watching reservation, and rental car remain confirmed, while the airline offers either the earlier flight at no added cost or a 2:50 p.m. one-stop return for $74 more per traveler.

events.continuity_hook: The preferred response to the airline schedule change is settled, leaving the flight exchange, car timing, and itinerary record to be updated together.
events.interaction_goal: Accept the replacement flight without losing the existing outbound, verify the new ticket total and seat assignments, extend the rental-car return time, and issue an updated chronological itinerary with the revised trip cost.
events.scenario_brief: Maya and her partner have chosen the 2:50 p.m. one-stop return for an added $148 total, keeping the trip below the $3,400 target. The airline change has not yet been accepted, and the rental-car reservation still shows a noon return even though a 12:45 p.m. drop-off would be more appropriate. Both lodging reservations and the Friday whale-watching time are unchanged.

events.continuity_hook: A new two-night client trip begins with complete flight timing, local transportation, and lodging geography unresolved.
events.interaction_goal: Identify workable Sunday outbound and Tuesday return windows, compare airport-to-client transportation costs, and determine which lodging area minimizes transfers while staying within the airfare and room limits.
events.scenario_brief: Maya needs to travel from Minneapolis to Columbus for a Monday afternoon project kickoff and Tuesday meetings ending at 4:00 p.m. She can leave Sunday after 3:00 p.m. and must return Tuesday night. Airfare may not exceed $650, lodging is capped at $240 per night before tax, and the client office is near Easton Town Center. No reservations have been made, and she is unsure whether an airport hotel or an Easton property will produce the simpler two-day schedule.

events.continuity_hook: The destination airport, lodging area, and ground-transportation approach are established, so the flight choice now turns on arrival quality and a realistic Tuesday departure.
events.interaction_goal: Compare complete itineraries, baggage charges, connection details, total travel time, and Tuesday airport margins; rule out any pairing that cannot be reached reliably; and select a round trip under the airfare ceiling.
events.scenario_brief: Easton has been chosen as the practical lodging area, with rideshares planned instead of a rental car. A $438 nonstop leaves Minneapolis at 5:10 p.m. Sunday and arrives at 8:03 p.m.; a $367 one-stop arrives at 10:41 p.m. Tuesday returns include a $512 round-trip pairing departing at 6:35 p.m. and a $449 pairing departing at 5:15 p.m., which leaves little margin after the meeting and the drive to the airport.

events.continuity_hook: Flight dates and transfer windows are fixed, leaving the true lodging totals, morning access, meal costs, and Tuesday luggage arrangements to determine the hotel.
events.interaction_goal: Calculate two-night totals with tax, breakfast, and expected rideshares; confirm Sunday late arrival and Tuesday luggage storage; assess the walking routes; and choose a refundable room within the nightly cap.
events.scenario_brief: The $512 nonstop round trip with the 6:35 p.m. Tuesday return is selected. Three Easton hotels are available for Sunday and Monday nights: a $239 nightly property across from the client office with breakfast included, a $207 hotel fifteen minutes away by rideshare, and a $224 hotel inside the shopping district that charges $18 for breakfast and is a twelve-minute walk from the office. Estimated lodging taxes are 17.5 percent, and Maya will need luggage held after Tuesday checkout.

events.continuity_hook: All trip components are selected, but ticketing, the refundable room reservation, arrival notation, and final timing reconciliation remain incomplete.
events.interaction_goal: Reconcile the Sunday-through-Tuesday dates and costs, ticket the expiring flights, reserve the hotel with the correct arrival time and luggage request, and assemble one confirmed itinerary including cancellation terms and the Tuesday airport departure plan.
events.scenario_brief: Maya has selected the $239 hotel across from the client office, totaling about $562 after tax for two nights, and the $512 nonstop flights. Estimated airport rideshares add $68, bringing the projected trip total to $1,142. The flight fare expires at midnight, the room can be canceled until 6:00 p.m. two days before arrival, and the hotel needs notice of the expected 8:45 p.m. Sunday check-in.
